text.text: Customers send requests through the form. Triage them on the board, link the answer article and attach feature requests to the feedback list.
Tickets
Feedback
Help articles
Urgent and high priority
A good reply is short, specific and kind. Most people writing to support are already annoyed; the quickest fix for that is a clear next step.
Greet the person by name and repeat the problem in one line.
Give the fix or the next step first.
Link the help article if one exists.
Say when they will hear from you next.
Mark the ticket Waiting if you need their reply.
A worked example

"Hi Petra, thanks for flagging the tax on your invoice. The rate was applied to the wrong region; I have corrected it and you will see a revised invoice within the hour. Details are in the Billing article linked below. I will check back tomorrow morning to make sure it looks right."
Before you send
The problem is repeated in one line
The fix or next step comes first
A date or time for the next contact is named
Triage decides who looks at a ticket next, not who is right. Apply the rule that matches, set the priority, and move on.
Urgent: customers cannot book or get paid. Reply within the hour.
High: a feature is broken for one customer. Reply the same day.
Normal: questions and requests. Reply within a day.
Low: ideas. Acknowledge within three days.
When rules collide

If a ticket is both a feature idea and a bug, split it: the bug goes in the ticket queue at its own priority and the idea goes to Feedback, linked back to the original. Count the ticket against the feedback row so the demand score reflects real people asking.
